solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Deceive graduate (male) left to divide drink (9)

indicatorNotes.to divide: something that divides a thing splits it in two, so the L goes between two parts of the drink

blocks.note: Bachelor of Arts, the usual crossword graduate
standard abbreviation
slang for alcohol, split before its last letter to take the L
standard abbreviation, placed inside the drink

annotation.surface: A male graduate walks out, leaving someone else to split the bar bill.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracketed "(male)" looks like a parenthetical aside about the graduate, but it is a separate piece of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is informal, with a flavour of dazzling someone with confusing talk until they are fooled.

entries.clue: Uneven politician blocking purchase (5)

indicatorNotes.blocking: a thing that blocks a passage sits inside it, so the politician lodges within the purchase

blocks.note: a good buy is a purchase; it opens after BU to take the politician
Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: An erratic politician stands in the way of a sale going through.
annotation.walkthrough: "Uneven" reads as a description of the politician's temperament, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a surface or ride full of rises and dips; it stretches to mean erratic, as the surface implies.

entries.clue: Accountants in thin fog given unsuitable roles (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the accountants are placed literally in the fog, surrounded by it

blocks.note: mist is a thinner fog; it opens after MIS
CA = chartered accountant; plural CAs

annotation.surface: Accountants lost in a haze have been put into jobs they are not fit for.
annotation.walkthrough: The plural matters: accountants gives two letters plus S, which is where the answer's second S comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre and film usage: actors are cast in parts, and the prefix mis- marks the casting as wrong for them.

entries.clue: State of being shot: awful lapse once involving church (11)

indicatorNotes.awful: something awful is badly done, so these letters are badly ordered and must be rearranged
indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to wrap up or enfold, so the rearranged letters surround the church

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
Church of England, sitting inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Someone recalls a dreadful slip-up in church that ended in a shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shot" is not gunfire: shot silk is woven so that its colour changes as the light moves.
annotation.definitionFit: Defined by a textile sense: shot fabric shimmers with shifting colours, which is the milky, iridescent quality named after the opal.

entries.clue: Chime cut short in unknown bishop’s capital (6)

indicatorNotes.cut short: a word cut short has had its tail snipped off, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.in: the shortened word sits inside the pair of letters around it

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
chime = agree, as views that chime; minus its last E
chess notation for bishop; the 's joins it to capital

annotation.surface: A bell rings abruptly in a mysterious bishop's city.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chime" is not a bell: opinions that chime agree with each other.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is the capital city of Croatia.

entries.clue: English story plugging box, an ornamental shrub (7) (8)

indicatorNotes.plugging: a plug fills a hole, so the story fills a gap inside the box word

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
to spar is to box; it opens after SPA
a story can be a fib, a lie

annotation.surface: An English tale is stuffed into a box alongside a decorative bush.
annotation.walkthrough: "Box" looks like a container, or even the box hedge beside the shrub; it is the verb, to fight with fists.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose definition by example: the word is really the method of training a tree or shrub flat against a wall, and by extension a shrub so trained.

entries.clue: Search leader of Oxford jazz group (5)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader goes at the front, so take the first letter

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
first letter

annotation.surface: Someone is hunting for the frontman of an Oxford jazz band.
annotation.walkthrough: "Leader" suggests the bandleader in the surface, but it only takes one letter of Oxford.
annotation.definitionFit: Jazz slang: short for combination, a small band of a few players.

entries.clue: Reduced share of profit (3)

blocks.note: past tense of trimming prices or spending
the portion of the takings each partner is due

annotation.surface: Someone's slice of the profits has shrunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The two meanings run together to read as a single complaint about a smaller share.
annotation.definitionFit: The same word is both the verb's past form for making smaller and a noun for one's slice of the proceeds.

entries.clue: Beginning of aggression is feeding man’s anguish (7)

indicatorNotes.Beginning of: the beginning of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.feeding: food goes into a mouth, so these letters go into the man

blocks.note: first letter
used as it stands
man = male; it opens after MAL to take the other letters

annotation.surface: Aggression gnawing at a man is the root of his torment.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in "man’s" is not part of the wordplay; read the clue as 'man's anguish', with the man as the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the word means a vague unease or sense of being unwell, a milder cousin of anguish.

entries.clue: Primate of old contacted sick aunt (5-4)

indicatorNotes.sick: something sick is out of sorts, so the aunt's letters are out of order

blocks.note: O = old, standard abbreviation
to ring someone is to phone, to contact them
anagram of AUNT

annotation.surface: An archbishop of former times got in touch with his ailing aunt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Primate" wants to be an archbishop, the churchman who fits the old-fashioned family scene, but it is the ape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this great ape of Borneo and Sumatra is one of the primates.

entries.clue: Essential article finally adorning wild horse (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally comes at the end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: a must = something essential
the indefinite article
last letter

annotation.surface: A must-have finishing touch decorates an untamed horse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Adorning" looks like a container indicator, but only its final letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the free-roaming horse of the American West, descended from Spanish stock.

entries.clue: Bone takeaways originally included in Spanish dish (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: what something was originally is how it started, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.included in: the letter is included in the dish, placed within it

blocks.note: the Valencian rice dish; it opens after PA
first letter

annotation.surface: A takeaway order of paella turns up with a bone in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about a takeaway meal, so "Bone" reads as a fishbone in the food rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The anatomical name, from Latin for a small dish, of the kneecap.

entries.clue: The old answer? Yes, long ago! (3)

blocks.note: an archaic affirmative reply
the older English form of an affirmative

annotation.surface: A question and its reply: what did people once say? The affirmative, in days of old.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same archaic word, so the clue appears to answer its own question.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaism: the old word for yes, still heard in 'yeas and nays' when votes are counted.

entries.clue: Endless translation of Latin verse by head of Greek (11)

indicatorNotes.translation of: a translation renders words into a new form, so the letters take a new order
indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
first letter, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A classics student grinds through an interminable translation of Latin poetry, then some Greek.
annotation.walkthrough: The classroom picture makes "Endless" read as a complaint about the task rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lasting for ever, without end.

entries.clue: Marvellous rise of a pastry dish’s overlying layers (11)

indicatorNotes.rise of: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, back to front

blocks.note: super = marvellous
A + TART'S, the S of the possessive included; read upward

annotation.surface: A wonderful pie rises in its dish with layer upon layer of pastry.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive S is part of the letters, which is easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A geological term: the plural of a layer lying above another, the reverse of substrata.

entries.clue: Find fault with a course for listeners (6)

indicatorNotes.for listeners: what is meant for listeners is what the ear hears, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a tack is a sailing course set at an angle to the wind

annotation.surface: Someone criticises a lecture series put on for an audience.
annotation.walkthrough: "Course" suggests a lecture course, with listeners as its students; in sailing it is the line a boat holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: to criticise someone's work or argument sharply, as if assaulting it.

entries.clue: High-level current worker? One introducing business (9)

indicatorNotes.introducing: whoever introduces something comes before it, so the one precedes business

blocks.note: the worker ant, crossword's standard worker
Roman numeral one
trade = business, commerce

annotation.surface: An electricity worker high up a pylon is launching a company.
annotation.walkthrough: "Current" hints at electricity, and "High-level" at seniority; it is an air current high in the atmosphere.
annotation.definitionFit: A meteorological term: winds blowing high above the trade winds and in the opposite direction.

entries.clue: Partner of this man destroyed temple (8)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: a building destroyed is knocked apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: this man = he
anagram of TEMPLE

annotation.surface: An accomplice of this man has pulled a temple down, like a biblical tale.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a news report of a crime; "Partner" looks like an accomplice.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for a wife or helper, from a misreading of 'an help meet for him' in Genesis.

entries.clue: Present-day tennis star securing entrance to this old US prison (8)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the star holds the letter inside
indicatorNotes.entrance to: the entrance is the way in, the first letter

blocks.note: Carlos Alcaraz, the Spanish champion; opens after ALCA
first letter

annotation.surface: A modern tennis champion guards the gates of a famous former American jail.
annotation.walkthrough: "Securing" fits the prison scene, locking someone up, which hides that it is a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the island jail in San Francisco Bay, closed in 1963.

entries.clue: Figure from Rhode Island in complicated situation (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the state is caught in the situation, surrounded by it

blocks.note: a tangle is a mess; it opens after T
US state abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone from Rhode Island has got into a real mess.
annotation.walkthrough: "Figure" looks like a person from Rhode Island; it is a shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the three-sided shape is a geometric figure.

entries.clue: The writer’s workforce, at first so exceptionally huge (7)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first is at the start, so take each word's first letter

blocks.note: the writer is = I am, contracted
the workforce = the men, the workers
first letters of so and exceptionally

annotation.surface: An author boasts that their staff are exceptionally large.
annotation.walkthrough: "The writer" is the setter speaking of themself, and the 's is 'is', not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vast, enormous.

entries.clue: French native in British college (6)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Eton College, the English boarding school

annotation.surface: A Frenchman is studying at a British college.
annotation.walkthrough: "In" looks like a container indicator, but the pieces simply join; it links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a native of Brittany, the region of north-west France.

entries.clue: Asian garments taken in by abstemious imperial supporter (7)

indicatorNotes.taken in by: to be taken in is to be admitted inside, so the garments go within the other letters

blocks.note: TT = teetotal; it splits in two around the garments
the wrapped dresses of South Asia

annotation.surface: A sober royalist is fooled by some Indian robes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Taken in" reads as deceived, which suits the surface, but it is a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A supporter of the tsar, Russia's emperor, and so of imperial rule.

entries.clue: One who succeeds, keeping extremely fine young beast (6)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the heir holds the letters inside
indicatorNotes.extremely: at the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: an heir succeeds to a title; it opens after HEI
outer letters of fine

annotation.surface: A successful person holds on to a very fine young animal.
annotation.walkthrough: "One who succeeds" suggests a winner; it is one who succeeds to a title or estate.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a young cow that has not yet had a calf.

entries.clue: Character that’s equal to the piano tuner? (11)

blocks.note: one's nature or disposition
piano tuners use the 'equal' system, dividing the octave into twelve equal steps

annotation.surface: Someone asks what sort of personality is a match for the piano tuner.
annotation.walkthrough: "Equal to" looks like 'a match for'; to a piano tuner, equal temperament is the tuning system.
annotation.definitionFit: The word covers both a person's disposition and, in music, a system of tuning; equal temperament is the standard one.

entries.clue: Cut duties, withdrawing the first and last (3)

indicatorNotes.withdrawing the first and last: withdrawing pulls something out, here the first and last letters

blocks.note: duties are taxes; lose the outer T and S

annotation.surface: A government cuts taxes, scrapping the first and last of them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as tax policy; the trimming applies to the letters of the word itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Journalistic usage: headlines use the word for cutting jobs or budgets, from chopping with the tool.

entries.clue: Keen always for poets to collect silver (5)

indicatorNotes.to collect: to collect something is to gather it in, so the poetic word takes the silver inside

blocks.note: e'er = ever, a poetic contraction; opens after E
chemical symbol, from Latin argentum

annotation.surface: Enthusiastic poets are forever gathering silver.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of the poetic contraction is ignored, as punctuation always is in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone enthusiastic and impatient to act.

entries.clue: Set aside a sparkler ultimately like a ring (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: a court sets aside a ruling or marriage by cancelling it
used as it stands
last letter

annotation.surface: Someone puts away a diamond that turned out, in the end, to be just a ring.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sparkler" evokes a diamond ring, which chimes with the definition, but it contributes only a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin anulus, a little ring: the word means ring-shaped, as in an annular eclipse.

entries.clue: Nonprofessional drama lacking introduction (3)

indicatorNotes.lacking introduction: an introduction comes first, so lacking it means losing the first letter

blocks.note: a stage drama; its opening P goes

annotation.surface: An amateur theatre production that skips the opening scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints an amateur dramatic society, which is why "Nonprofessional" sits so naturally.
annotation.definitionFit: A church sense widened: not ordained, and hence not expert, as in a layman's view.

entries.clue: Blooming American interrupting Highland dance! (7)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so the American goes inside the dance

blocks.note: the Highland fling, a lively Scottish dance; opens after FL
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: An American barges in on a Scottish dance, to exasperated cries.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blooming" is not flowering but a mild British curse, a polite stand-in for bloody.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: both are mild intensifiers used in exasperation, softened substitutes for bloody.

entries.clue: Part of novel Egyptians lament (5)

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is only part of the following words, a run of their letters

blocks.note: novEL EGYptians

annotation.surface: A passage from a novel in which Egyptians mourn.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lament" looks like a verb for the Egyptians; it is the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A poem or song of mourning for the dead is a lament in verse.

entries.clue: Persian prophet from wizard place brought back chicken for cooking (9)

indicatorNotes.brought back: to bring something back is to return it the way it came, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: the land of the Wizard of Oz, read backwards
a bird raised for roasting

annotation.surface: A mystic returns from a magical land bringing a chicken for the pot.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wizard" chimes with the prophet but points to the Wizard of Oz's land.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Iranian prophet, also called Zarathustra, who founded Zoroastrianism.
